proposed_comments.title: Reject unusable inspector ports during manifest parsing

confidence.rationale: The changed parser accepts every Int32 debugPort, while TCP inspector ports must be 1 through 65535 and port 0 cannot be rediscovered by this host.

proposed_comments.title: Fail closed when an entry-point segment disappears

confidence.rationale: The current catch returns false, which means trusted/not-a-reparse-point, after File.GetAttributes could not verify a segment because it disappeared during the containment walk.

proposed_comments.title: Report exhaustion when the final line reaches the byte cap

confidence.rationale: The notice flag is set only when a later line is suppressed, so an exact-cap final line leaves BudgetExhausted false despite TotalLoggedBytes reaching the configured maximum.

proposed_comments.body:
### Report exhaustion when the final line reaches the byte cap

**Severity:** `low`

`BudgetExhausted` remains false when the last emitted line reaches the cap exactly because the notice flag is only set by a later suppressed line. Deriving the status from the accumulated byte count keeps the public state accurate at EOF; please cover the exact-cap case.

```suggestion
    public bool BudgetExhausted => _totalLoggedBytes >= _maxTotalBytes;
```

proposed_comments.title: Treat bare carriage returns as stderr line terminators

confidence.rationale: The branch discards carriage returns, so inputs such as first\rsecond\r are concatenated until EOF instead of being forwarded and rate-accounted as separate records.

proposed_comments.body:
### Treat bare carriage returns as stderr line terminators

**Severity:** `medium`

The current branch discards `\r`, so progress-style stderr such as `first\rsecond\r` becomes one concatenated record and bypasses per-line forwarding/accounting. Emit and reset here; the following `\n` in CRLF input will only produce the already-ignored empty line. Please add a bare-carriage-return regression test.

```suggestion
            EmitLine();
            ResetLine();
```

proposed_comments.title: Do not enable single-reader channel optimizations

confidence.rationale: EnqueueNotification calls Reader.TryRead on producer threads while ConsumeNotificationsAsync also reads, so SingleReader=true contradicts the actual access pattern.

proposed_comments.body:
### Do not enable single-reader channel optimizations

**Severity:** `medium`

`EnqueueNotification` reads from the channel when the bounded queue is full while the consumer task is also reading. Declaring `SingleReader = true` enables assumptions that are invalid for that access pattern and can make the overflow path unsafe.

```suggestion
            SingleReader = false,
```

proposed_comments.title: Serialize RPC target registration

confidence.rationale: ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd may run a value factory more than once, and this factory mutates StreamJsonRpc by registering a target before the dictionary chooses the retained value.

proposed_comments.body:
### Serialize RPC target registration

**Severity:** `high`

`ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd` may execute this value factory more than once for the same method. Because `AddRpcMethodTarget` also registers the method with StreamJsonRpc, concurrent request/notification registration can create duplicate or ambiguous targets. Serialize the dictionary check, RPC registration, and dictionary update under one lock, and add a concurrent-registration regression test.

proposed_comments.title: Bound concurrently executing inbound requests

confidence.rationale: Each StreamJsonRpc request can enter the handler concurrently and the existing ServerBusy code is otherwise unused, leaving no admission limit against a faulty extension.

proposed_comments.body:
### Bound concurrently executing inbound requests

**Severity:** `high`

Every inbound request can currently start a handler task immediately, so a faulty extension can accumulate unbounded in-flight work and exhaust the host. Add a small non-blocking request budget, return `LocalRpcException` with `ServerBusy` when it is full, release the slot in `finally`, and cover saturation with concurrent requests.

proposed_comments.title: Retry notification admission after the consumer wins the race

confidence.rationale: When TryWrite observes a full queue but the consumer removes the final item before TryRead, TryRead returns false and this return silently drops the new notification without incrementing the counter.

proposed_comments.title: Isolate disconnect event subscribers

confidence.rationale: A multicast delegate stops invoking later subscribers when an earlier subscriber throws, and this callback runs during transport teardown.

proposed_comments.title: Make StreamJsonRpc dispatch NativeAOT-safe
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The safe repair requires a coordinated central StreamJsonRpc package upgrade and generated target metadata changes across other PowerToys consumers; the central dependency/version files and those consumers are not part of PR 49323, so there is no self-contained current RIGHT-side patch that can be offered here.
proposed_comments.companion_rationale: This is a cross-repository-consumer dependency migration rather than a localized replacement in one changed hunk.

confidence.rationale: The AOT-compatible ViewModels project registers local methods with MethodInfo/AddLocalRpcMethod and sends parameter objects through object[]; pinned StreamJsonRpc 2.21.69 lacks RpcTargetMetadata and NamedArgs.

proposed_comments.body:
### Make the StreamJsonRpc dispatch paths NativeAOT-safe

**Severity:** `high`

`Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels` opts into AOT compatibility, but the new transport registers inbound handlers through reflection-based `AddLocalRpcMethod` and sends named parameter objects through `object[]`/`InvokeCoreAsync`. The pinned StreamJsonRpc 2.21.69 package does not provide the NativeAOT-safe `RpcTargetMetadata` and `NamedArgs` APIs, so a trimmed CmdPal build can lose or fail the binder metadata even though an ordinary Debug build passes. Please coordinate an upgrade to a StreamJsonRpc version with those APIs, register local targets using generated metadata, use the `NamedArgs` parameter-object invocation overload, and add an AOT publish smoke test that exercises one inbound call and one outbound parameter-object request.
